name: Production planning and scheduling
one_line: Planning records for what will be made, in what quantity, on which plant or line, and by which dates: demand plans, master production schedules, MRP and planned-order runs, finite-capacity schedules, sequencing boards, material-availability reviews and release decisions. Placeholder template (J-IND, full J-DEPTH): manufacturing keeps fields empty pending R1c.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: SECONDING, NOT MINTING. The manufacturing schema already proposes `product` for the physical article, formulation or SKU being planned. Planning records contain many products; a product is legal only from a labelled item/part/material role, never from a customer name or commodity word.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Useful below site or planning period when demand and capacity branches are maintained by product family; a multi-product schedule must not copy one row's value to every member.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: A labelled Product, Material, Part, SKU or Finished Good slot is direct evidence; an item-like token in a filename or description remains possible until item-master context validates its role.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: SECONDING, NOT MINTING. Manufacturing proposes `site` for a facility that performs production or controls an asset. Planning demonstrates plant and production-location roles; Photos `location` is the capture role and cannot replace the facility-about role.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Useful when a planning corpus spans several plants; flatten for a single-site corpus. A customer, supplier or delivery address is not a manufacturing site fact.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: A labelled Plant, Production Site, Planning Plant or Manufacturing Location slot joined to capacity/order rows can be direct evidence; addresses and organization names in prose remain possible.

proposed_fields.example: master production schedule / MRP run / capacity plan
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: SECONDING, NOT MINTING. Reuse manufacturing's proposed `record_type` for planning-artifact function: demand plan, master schedule, planned-order run, finite-capacity plan, shortage review and release board. Do not mint `planning_record_type`.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: A function level can separate schedule, MRP, capacity and release artifacts beneath the planning subject when the corpus has several functions; a filename word does not establish it.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: A labelled title and matching planning tables or review agenda support the function. Extension, branding and isolated words do not.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: No canonical field expresses the planning horizon or bucket the schedule is ABOUT. `creation_date` is byte metadata, `version_family` identifies versions, and `batch_lot` is produced quantity rather than a horizon. This proposal covers weekly, monthly, quarterly or rolling horizons; R1c may replace it with one neutral period key.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Useful below site for multiple frozen or rolling horizons; not time-first, because the planning subject or site should contextualize it and snapshot date is not the demand horizon.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Validation requires a labelled Planning Horizon, Schedule Period, Requirement Period, MRP Run Horizon or Bucket field with planning-table context. Filename dates and filesystem timestamps remain possible.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: No existing proposal names the recurring production resource at line/work-centre level. `asset` names an enduring maintained or calibrated equipment item, while a line or cell is a capacity/sequencing resource containing many assets. R1c should widen `asset` with a resource role or admit this exact key; no machine-specific synonym is minted.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Useful only where capacity plans genuinely branch by stable line or cell; it remains search evidence for site-wide S&OP or aggregate plans.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Validation requires a labelled Line, Work Centre, Cell, Resource or Production Unit column joined to operation sequence and capacity/availability data. A machine name or asset tag alone is never enough.

template.why: Empty by placeholder contract: manufacturing declares no legal field rows, and `planning_period` and `production_line` are proposals pending R1c. Subject to that decision, planning recommends site → planning_period → product → production_line (when line-primary) → record_type, with a product-family or site aggregate branch for S&OP. This differs from manufacturing's production branch product → batch_lot → record_type because planning is many-order and horizon-led: a planned order is a proposal, not a produced lot, and capacity assignments are not execution facts. It is not time-first: 00 says, "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." The user may reverse, remove or flatten dimensions after facts are validated.

collides_with.signal: SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Production-Schedule-and-Work-Order-Release_2026-08.xlsx` contains planned multi-order rows and a released-order sheet. THIS ROW claims planned rows expressing demand, quantities, dates, capacity and release proposals without actual operator/completion evidence; production-record claims the same bytes only where a single order/batch has routed steps populated with actuals, signoffs, yield or scrap. Conversely, this row must not treat an executed traveller as a schedule because it contains planned columns, and production-record must not treat planned dates and capacities as completed work. Many planned orders versus populated actual execution is the discriminator.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `AX410_Routing-and-Setup-Instruction_RevC.pdf` carries operation sequence, standard times and setup parameters shared with a schedule's routing inputs. THIS ROW claims the bytes only when those values are assigned to multiple planned orders, dates, capacity buckets or sequencing decisions; work-instruction claims them when they define a reusable controlled method under revision/effective-date furniture without a planning horizon or order list. Conversely, a revision-controlled method is not a capacity plan merely because it contains times, and a schedule's operation assignment is not a reusable instruction.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `AX410_Routing-and-Setup-Instruction_RevC.pdf` can be read as a planning input or engineering definition. THIS ROW claims it only when the engineering values are consumed in a multi-order demand/capacity/schedule structure; engineering claims it when controlled routing, process definition or design revision is the subject and planned dates/quantities are absent. Conversely, this row must not infer a design change from a scheduled operation, and engineering must not claim a planning board from a drawing or standard-time table alone.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Inbound-Component-Availability-and-Delivery-Board.xlsx` has component, due-date, supplier, receipt and status columns that resemble a material plan. THIS ROW claims the bytes only when the workbook joins shortages to planned orders, manufacturing horizon, capacity or release decisions; logistics claims them when inbound custody, purchase-order delivery, warehouse receipt or carrier status is the subject. Conversely, a component shortage mention does not make a delivery board a production plan, and a manufacturing schedule must not absorb supplier/warehouse facts merely because supply is an input.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Plant-2_Schedule-Freeze-and-Release-Review.pptx` contains demand, supply, capacity and decisions. THIS ROW claims the slides when manufacturing horizon, product/site/line loads and planned-order exceptions are the subject; business_operations claims them when S&OP governance, management objectives, resource commitments or corporate decision controls are the subject. Conversely, a management deck is not a manufacturing schedule from a plant name alone, and manufacturing planning must not claim every executive forecast or decision presentation.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `AX410_Demand-and-Supply-Plan_2026-09.csv` can be included in a statutory or investor reporting packet. THIS ROW claims the operational planning table joining products, demand, planned supply, site and manufacturing constraints; corporate-regulatory-filings claims it when a filing wrapper, reporting period, sign-off and external disclosure obligation make the corporate submission the subject. Conversely, a corporate wrapper cannot donate planning facts to an unlabelled attachment, and an internal manufacturing plan is not a regulatory filing just because its values appear in one.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Plant-2_MPS_FY2026-Q3_RevB.xlsx` may be exported into a dispatch/fulfilment board with dates, quantities and routes. THIS ROW claims the bytes when they are planned manufacturing orders assigned to site/line/capacity before execution; logistics.route-dispatch claims them when shipment, vehicle, route, custody and delivery sequence govern. Conversely, planned production dates do not become transport dispatch dates, and a route board must not be called a manufacturing schedule because products and quantities recur.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Production-Planning-Decision-Log.docx` shares dated rows, resources, constraints and decisions with a construction site diary. THIS ROW claims it when the recurring object is planned manufacture across products, orders, lines and material/capacity constraints; construction_property.site-diary claims the same bytes when the object is a property/site, trade sequence, weather, subcontractor activity or built-work progress. Conversely, dates and resource names alone do not activate either side, and a factory address does not make a production planning record.

falls_through_to.why: A standalone schedule snapshot, planning decision note, release memo or routing extract with durable purpose but no complete product/site/horizon/capacity relation remains an independent record.
A delivery promise, material receipt, order acknowledgement or confirmation that lacks a manufacturing horizon and capacity/supply decision belongs in the transactional residual.
An unlabelled quantity/date table, mixed planned-versus-actual export, weak OCR board or ambiguous S&OP deck should be reviewed rather than assigned a plan or execution fact.
A planning-board screenshot whose OCR cannot establish its own product/site/horizon structure may be useful context but should remain temporary until accepted grouping or clearer evidence exists.
An unreadable ERP/MRP/APS export or encrypted planning packet must be represented safely without inferring a schedule from its filename or archive name.

sensitivity_why: Production plans can expose demand forecasts, customer requirements, product mix, plant capacity, bottlenecks, supplier dependencies, shortages, launch timing and commercially sensitive sequencing. A management or public schedule may be less sensitive, but publication cannot be inferred from file type or title. The catalogue assigns only potentially_sensitive; P7 owns handling and model-access policy, and worker, customer, supplier and organization names remain role observations rather than destination dimensions.
open_question: NJ-PLAN-1: should `planning_period` be admitted as a shared neutral period key, or should planning horizons remain search-only while the user organizes by product/site? `creation_date` and `version_family` do not express the horizon. NJ-PLAN-2: should `production_line` be a distinct canonical resource key, or should manufacturing's proposed `asset` carry line/work-centre roles with a canonical role split? A line is a capacity resource, not necessarily one maintained machine. NJ-PLAN-3: should a planned-order identifier receive a separate key, reuse the existing `work_order` proposal from execution/maintenance, or remain evidence only? Reusing it risks making planned and executed states indistinguishable. NJ-PLAN-4: when an S&OP deck carries both management governance and manufacturing supply/capacity tables, should R1c author schema-level coactivation while this template keeps `also_holds_with` empty? NJ-PLAN-5: where the same workbook contains planned rows and actual execution sheets, should sheet-level evidence permit both planning and production-record activation, or require a primary user decision? NJ-PLAN-6: which ERP/MRP/APS export formats receive approved local extractors; until then opaque exports remain indexed-but-unreadable.
